note: Based on Sjöstedt's (1900) description of this species, original in Latin and German; the alate section follows the specimens and notes of Haviland and others. The total length and the length of the head with the nasus of the major soldier, the width of the queen's abdomen and the head width of the worker are damaged in the scanned text and are not recorded; synonymic and bibliographic citations, figure numbers and locality records have been omitted, as well as the long English note by Weale on the acid secretion of the soldier quoted in the original.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Major soldier: head circular in dorsal view, pale red-yellow, the nasus distinctly darker but not much so; nasus long and very slender, from the antennal bases longer than the rest of the head by 1/6, only rather weakly upturned, so that it is not quite in the same line as the head; antennae 14-segmented, segments 3 and 4 long, the middle segments twice as long as wide, becoming shorter towards the apex; anterior margin of the pronotum incised. Minor soldier: distinctly smaller and more slender, the nasus relatively longer, the antennae also longer, the boundary between segments 3 and 4 often indistinct. Total length of the minor soldier 4, length of the head with the nasus 1.7; the measurements of the major soldier are damaged in the scanned text and are not recorded.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head elongate, oval to quadrate, reddish brown or paler, distinctly concave in the middle, with three white lines meeting centrally, of which the occipital line is broader and extends to the labrum; labrum with a brown spot on each side; the whole base of the mandibles, the sides of the head, the labrum, the labial palps and the antennae pale yellow; anterior margin of the pronotum with a median incision. Total length 5.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Upper surface rusty; mouthparts, antennae, legs, labrum, the whole pronotum and the underside yellow; abdominal spiracles dark, forming small dots on each side of the sternites; abdominal tergites with yellow margins. Head slightly longer than wide, with a depression on the frons dividing into two branches towards the mouth, and a small yellow fontanelle spot in the middle; labrum swollen; compound eyes large, almost circular, rather flat; ocelli large, circular or broadly oval, separated from the compound eyes by slightly less than their own diameter; antennae 15-segmented, sometimes 16-segmented, segment 2 shorter than segment 3. Wings dull yellow-grey, costal vein red-yellow; an orange-yellow stripe beneath the subcosta from the middle to the tip of the costa; the media gives off very distinct small accessory veins into the subcostal area, the accessory veins often curved, not reaching the subcosta but directed towards the wing apex. Wing expanse 38–44, body length with wings 19–23, wing length 18–20 and width 5, body with head 9–10.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: The sides of the abdomen of the queen are yellow-white, densely covered with fine hairs and scattered with brown, ill-defined small dots; abdomen 15 long. The nest is a circular earth mound standing on the ground, whose outer chambers are filled with comminuted gravel; the original states that its biology is very similar to that of a closely related species, which likewise builds circular epigeal mounds.
